questions.stem: What type of defect is seen in HNPCC?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mismatch repair
  • The type of defect seen in HNPCC (Hereditary Non-Polyposis Colorectal Cancer) is: C. Mismatch repair

questions.stem: A 30 year old male presented with fatiguability for one year . Evaluation showed mild anemia, massive splenomegaly with TLC 1,50,000/microliters, neutrophil 60%, eosinophil 4%, lymphocyte15%. Also seen myeloblast , myelocytes , metamyelocytes and bands. M-E ratio is 18:1 . What is most sensitive investigation?
questions.solutionHtml:
FISH and PCR
  • Given the patient's clinical presentation with fatigability, mild anemia, massive splenomegaly, and abnormal peripheral blood smear findings, the most likely diagnosis is chronic myeloid leukemia (CML).
  • The presence of a markedly elevated total leukocyte count (TLC), myeloblasts, myelocytes, metamyelocytes, and bands on the peripheral smear suggests a myeloproliferative disorder.
  • To confirm the diagnosis of CML and detect the specific genetic abnormality associated with the disease, the most sensitive investigation is FISH and PCR.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 622-624

questions.stem: A patient presented with webbed neck, shield chest and short stature. Identify the diagnosis in this case scenario?
questions.solutionHtml:
Turner syndrome
  • Based on the presented features of webbed neck, shield chest, and short stature, the most likely diagnosis in this case scenario is Turner syndrome.

questions.stem: A research scholar while studying cytoskeleton from a chronic alcoholic patient with decreased liver span, came across several strands of fibrous proteins that are wound together as a stable structure and distribute tensile forces across cells in the tissue. The records indicate that his liver biopsy showed hepatocytes with reddish inclusions. Which one of the following structures is best suited?
questions.solutionHtml:
Intermediate filaments
  • The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Alcoholic liver cirrhosis, with the presence of Mallory Denk Bodies.
  • Mallory denk bodies are intermediate filaments.They  are  made  up  of  tangled  skeins  of  intermediate filaments  such  as  keratins  8  and  18  in  complex  with  other proteins  such  as  ubiquitin.

questions.stem: Patient with generalized fatigue, tiredness. Primary clinical examination is uneventful. Normal TLC and DLC. No immature cells seen. Superficial discrete lymph nodes enlarged. On biopsy showed effaced architecture, indented nucleus, prominent nucleolus containing atypical cells. CD10 and BCL2 positive?
questions.solutionHtml:
Follicular
  • Based on the presented clinical findings and histopathological features, the most likely diagnosis in this case scenario is A. Follicular lymphoma.
  • Follicular lymphoma is a type of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma characterized by the involvement of B cells. The clinical presentation of generalized fatigue, tiredness, and the presence of enlarged superficial discrete lymph nodes is consistent with the typical manifestations of follicular lymphoma.

questions.stem: Patient with mediastinal mass was diagnosed with red cell aplasia. What is the most probable cause of aplasia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thymoma
  • The most probable cause of red cell aplasia in a patient with a mediastinal mass is C. Thymoma.
  • Thymomas can be associated with various paraneoplastic syndromes, including pure red cell aplasia (PRCA).
  • Thymomas can produce factors or antibodies that suppress erythropoiesis, leading to red cell aplasia. The mechanism of PRCA in thymoma may involve autoimmune or immunological processes that disrupt normal red blood cell production.

questions.stem: Pap smear with hyperchromatic nuclei and pleomorphism with low maturation index involving complete epithelial lining but not involving the basement membrane. What is this called?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dysplasia
  • Given the case scenario points towards the presence of carcinoma in situ. However, since it is not given in the options, dysplasia seems to be the best answer.

questions.stemHtml: A 34 year old woman presented with fever, migratory arthritis of lower large joints, tachycardia. Murmur is pansystolic. On echo Mitral regurgitation is present. The biopsy shows the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Aschoff body
  • The patient's clinical presentation with fever, migratory arthritis of lower large joints, tachycardia, and a pansystolic murmur is consistent with acute rheumatic fever.
  • The characteristic histological finding in ARF is the presence of Aschoff bodies.
  • Aschoff bodies are focal inflammatory lesions that consist of central areas of fibrinoid necrosis surrounded by a mixture of lymphocytes, plasma cells, histiocytes, and occasional multinucleated giant cells.
  • These lesions primarily affect the myocardium, particularly in the interventricular septum.

questions.stem: Poor prognostic marker for multiple myeloma is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Beta2- microglobulin
  • Beta2-microglobulin (B2M) is a protein that is normally present on the surface of many cells, including plasma cells.
  • In multiple myeloma, increased levels of B2M in the blood are associated with a poor prognosis.
  • Elevated B2M levels are indicative of more advanced disease and higher tumor burden. It is a marker of tumor mass and aggressiveness in multiple myeloma.

questions.stem: A 18 yr old male presented with gum bleeding and easy bruisability and fever for last 2 months. General examination finding were not specific except for significant pallor and petechial rash all over the body. HB 3 g/dl, TLC 1500/μL, platelet 1500o/μL. PBS: macrocytes corrected retic 0.5. Bone marrow exam showed fatty streak, absent megakaryocyte, no immature cells. What is the diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Idiopathic acquired Aplastic anemia
  • Given the case scenario of a young adolescent with gum bleed, fever and pancytopenia along with low retic count and fatty streaks points to the diagnosis of idiopathic acquired aplastic anemia.
  • Acquired aplastic anemia is a rare, serious blood disorder, due to failure of the bone marrow failure to produce blood cells.
